Topic: Three tau scenarios: nearly identical, moderate, wildly different
Story (story.md): Tau is the dial that says how different the segments really are; tiny tau means glue everything to the population mean, large tau means barely pool at all.

Topic: Shrinkage factor on the logit scale
Story (story.md): Shrinkage is a quantity I can read off the posterior: how far each segment got pulled from its own data toward the population mean.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Try: shrinkage_i = (independent_i - posterior_mean_i) / (independent_i - mu_posterior_mean).

Topic: Posterior on tau tracks the truth
Story (story.md): When segments are identical, the posterior on tau lands near zero and pooling is heavy. When segments really differ, tau lands away from zero and pooling is light.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Observe: posterior on tau concentrates near 0, 0.04, 0.15 respectively; average shrinkage ~1, ~0.4, <0.1. Image tau_learned.png.

Topic: Pooling strength is learned, not chosen

Topic: Prior on tau matters when N is small
Story (story.md): With lots of data the prior on tau is essentially irrelevant. With little data it is the strongest lever in the room.

Topic: Tight prior collapses toward pop mean, wide prior keeps no-pool shape
